allies.rationale_text: Systems-thinking gives abstraction the whole-machine view that lets high-level models capture interrelationships instead of static detail piles.
allies.source_quote: Systems thinking is intrinsically allied with abstraction
allies.affinity_rationale: Described as 'intrinsically allied with abstraction, serving as a discipline for seeing wholes' — strong foundational relationship where systems thinking provides the interrelationship view that makes abstraction productive.
allies.activation_condition: When modeling complex phenomena and need to see interrelationships and whole-system patterns rather than accumulating static data points

allies.rationale_text: First-principles-thinking keeps abstraction honest by rebuilding the model from facts rather than from inherited labels alone.
allies.source_quote: abstraction conflicts with first-principles-thinking when high-level labels hide untested assumptions
allies.affinity_rationale: Corrective complement — keeps abstraction honest by rebuilding from facts, but also carries an explicit tension ('high-level labels hide untested assumptions'), indicating a dual-nature relationship rather than pure synergy.
allies.activation_condition: When inherited high-level categories or labels may mask untested assumptions about the underlying structure that abstraction has preserved uncritically

allies.rationale_text: Simplification is the practical expression of abstraction when complexity is compressed into a clearer structure without losing what matters.
allies.affinity_rationale: Framed as an output aptitude of abstraction — 'find simplicity in complexity' — rather than a mechanism that strengthens abstraction itself. The relationship flows from abstraction producing simplification, not simplification powering abstraction.
allies.activation_condition: When complex systems need to be compressed into clearer structures for communication or action without losing essential relationships

antagonists.rationale_text: Theory-induced-blindness corrupts abstraction when the framework becomes a cage that forces reality to fit the model rather than revising the model to fit reality.
antagonists.source_quote: torture reality so that it fits your models
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Described as 'a primary antagonist' — corrupts abstraction when the framework forces reality to fit the model ('torture reality so that it fits your models') rather than revising the model to fit reality.
antagonists.activation_condition: When the abstract framework has become a comfortable lens that forces incoming evidence to conform rather than updating the model when reality diverges

structured_tensions.tension_text: Abstraction conflicts with first-principles-thinking when high-level labels hide untested assumptions that should have been stripped away before synthesis.
structured_tensions.source_quote: abstraction vs first-principles-thinking: abstraction conflicts with first-principles-thinking (first principles thinking) when high-level labels hide untested assumptions.
